children: Sinda Ltd. (NYSE: SIND) (the “Company” or “Sinda”) today announced that its common stock will be added to the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (“GDXJ”), effective at market close on September 18, 2026.

Sinda’s inclusion follows the Company’s initial public offering and listing on the New York Stock Exchange on June 26, 2026, marking another milestone in the Company’s evolution as a publicly traded precious metals company.

“Sinda’s inclusion in GDXJ represents an important step, less than three months after our NYSE listing this year,” said Daniel Muñiz, Executive Chairman. “We believe it will further enhance Sinda’s profile within the global precious metals investment community as we continue to advance the Sinda Project and execute our exploration and development strategy in what we believe to be one of the most important silver-gold discoveries in Mexico – if not the world.”

GDXJ provides investors with exposure to a portfolio of small- and mid-capitalization companies across the global gold and silver mining sectors. The Company believes its inclusion may increase Sinda’s visibility and exposure among institutional and other investors focused on the global precious metals sector.
For more information on GDXJ, please visit:

Sinda is a silver exploration and development company with mineral projects in Mexico, that has already identified an estimated 369 million silver-equivalent ounces of Inferred Mineral Resources and 16 million silver-equivalent ounces of Indicated Mineral Resources, plus incremental Exploration Targets of 452–484 million silver-equivalent ounces that, while conceptual in nature and insufficiently explored to estimate a mineral resource, offer line of sight to a base of more than 800 million silver-equivalent ounces on only 38% of the known veins drilled. Backed by experienced mining investors and a management team with deep Mexican operating experience, Sinda expects to execute an aggressive exploration and drilling program, and to construct its underground decline en route to commercial production.
